name: NAIAD
summary: NAIAD was a historical NaI(Tl) dark-matter experiment at Boulby, UK, using high-light-yield crystals and pulse-shape analysis to test WIMP nuclear recoils.
detection_principle: NaI scintillation timing statistically separates nuclear recoils. The low-background underground environment enables limits on dark-matter scattering cross sections.

sites.name: Boulby Underground Laboratory
sites.site_status: Experiment site; see the phase descriptions

status.label: Completed
status.evidence: The final paper explicitly identifies data taking from 2000 to 2003.

collaboration.name: UK Dark Matter Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Only verified representative institutions are listed, not a complete membership roster. See the collaboration pages and author affiliations in the references.

key_parameters.name: Crystals included
key_parameters.value: Two encapsulated and four unencapsulated crystals

results.summary: Final pulse-shape analysis and upper limits on WIMP cross sections were published.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
